newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to another record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to another record.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose to record highs Friday for the third time in a week.
Strength on Wall Street and funds flowing in from overseas helped lift the market, analysts and dealers said.
The IPC blue-chip index rose 41.85 points to a record 4,160.85. On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average soared 130.49 points to a record 7,435.78.

Felix Boni, research director at ING-Barings, said the momentum was helping Mexican stocks catch up to markets in other countries. "The bolsa had been an underperformer relative to Latin America," Boni said.
Investors were not concerned by the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on U.S. interest rates next month and Mexican mid-term elections on July 6.
In the broader market, gainers beat losers, 56-42, as volume was brisk at 142.9 million shares, dealers said.

Dealers said Telmex, which accounted for some 16 percent of all shares traded, drove the market most. The telecommunications giant gained 30 centavos (4 cents) to a record close in peso terms of 18.80 ($2.35).
Telmex ADRs climbed 3/4 on Wall Street to 47, a level not seen since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis. In February 1994, Telmex ADRs traded at more than 74.
Financial firm Bancomer also gained sharply at heavy trade to stand near the top on the leading gainers' list.

Financial stocks had lagged behind the market, and their second quarter reports should benefit from the downward trend in interest rates and inflation, said Francisco Blanco, research head at the Arka brokerage.
Bancomer's A class shares gained 15 centavos (2 cents) to 1.93 pesos (24 cents), while the more commonly traded B class ended up 17 centavos (2 cents) at 3.50 pesos (44 cents).
Financial firm Banacci climbed 48 centavos (6 cents) to 19.36 pesos ($2.42). Bancomer and Banacci are Mexico's two largest brokerage houses.
Retail stock Cifra did not take part, closing down 60 centavos (8 cents) to 13.00 pesos ($1.62) on what traders called a lukewarm reaction to the merger pact with Wal-Mart Stores Inc.

Looking ahead, analysts said the market could rally again next week but that the U.S. producer price report due on June 13 could dampen enthusiasm if evidence of inflation pushes bond market rates higher.
